theorem.statement:
For every \(h\geq 1\), the causal residual complexity is
\[
\rho(h)=B_h=\operatorname{Bell}(h).
\]
The upper bound is realized by the complete-prefix partition state.  For the matching lower bound, for each \(h\geq2\) there is one ordered binary prefix architecture with \(h\) nonfactual retained contexts, factual value \(S=0\), and every retained context intervening to set \(S=1\), such that every partition \(\pi\in\operatorname{Part}(\mathcal H)\) is a feasible preterminal prefix.  Its predecessor selector coordinates are indexed by the nonempty proper subsets of \([h]\).  Any two distinct such prefixes are separated by one common legal natural response-table suffix at a terminal binary variable \(Y\) and by a predecessor-normal conjunction \(\gamma^{\circ}\) whose retained contexts are exactly \(\mathcal H\), with no factual context adjoined.  Hence there is no uniformly coarser exact continuation quotient under the causal residual-distinguishability handle.  The existing \(\mathsf C_1\) upper bound \(B_h3^{(h-1)/3}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) remains valid; the equality \(\rho(h)=B_h\) is a state lower bound and does not assert an \(h\log h\) time lower bound or a lower bound for all reduced decision diagrams.
theorem.proof_tex:
By \texttt{thm:partition-continuation}, two feasible normalized prefixes with the same complete-prefix equality partition have the same legal continuation support, including the same terminal acceptance possibilities.  There are \(B_h=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) partitions of an \(h\)-element context set.  Thus the partition itself is an exact online continuation state and
\[
\rho(h)\leq B_h. \tag{1}
\]
It remains to prove that no uniform exact quotient uses fewer states in the worst case.

Fix \(h\geq2\), identify the retained worlds with \([h]\), and put
\[
\mathcal C_h=\{C:\varnothing\neq C\subsetneq[h]\}.
\]
Choose an arbitrary fixed order on \(\mathcal C_h\).  Consider, in this order, the endogenous binary variables
\[
S< (Z_C)_{C\in\mathcal C_h}<Y,
\qquad
\mathcal D_S=\mathcal D_{Z_C}=\mathcal D_Y=\{0,1\}.
\]
Fix the factual cell to be zero at every coordinate.  For \(j\in[h]\), define the intervention \(I_j\) by
\[
\operatorname{dom}(I_j)
=\{S\}\cup\{Z_C:C\in\mathcal C_h,\ j\in C\},
\qquad
I_j(S)=1,
\qquad
I_j(Z_C)=1\quad(j\in C). \tag{2}
\]
No \(I_j\) intervenes on \(Y\).  All these contexts are nonfactual because they set \(S=1\), whereas the factual cell has \(S=0\).  They are distinct: if \(j\neq j'\), then the coordinate \(Z_{\{j\}}\) belongs to the domain of \(I_j\) and not to that of \(I_{j'}\).

We next show that every partition of these same \(h\) contexts is reachable before \(Y\).  Fix a target partition \(\pi\) of \([h]\).  Set the factual row of \(S\) to zero.  Equation~(2) makes the \(I_j\)-world value of \(S\) equal to one for every \(j\), so their partition just after \(S\) is the one-block partition.  Process the selectors in their fixed order.  Immediately before \(Z_C\), let \(\tau\) be the current partition and, for each \(T\in\tau\), let \(q_T\) be the common complete predecessor tuple of the worlds indexed by \(T\).  Inductively, every \(T\) is a union of blocks of \(\pi\).  For every \(T\) containing at least one natural world at \(Z_C\), prescribe the response row
\[
 f_{Z_C}(q_T)=
 \begin{cases}
 0, & C\in\pi,\\
 \mathbf 1\{T\cap C\neq\varnothing\}, & C\notin\pi.
 \end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
Also prescribe zero on the factual predecessor tuple.  The latter prescription cannot conflict with a query-world prescription, because its \(S\)-coordinate is zero while every \(q_T\) has \(S=1\).  Distinct blocks \(T\) have distinct complete predecessor tuples by \texttt{def:prefix-partition}.  Therefore all rows in (3) are mutually consistent, and \texttt{ass:complete-predecessor-functions} permits them to be chosen independently; unlisted rows may be assigned zero.

If \(C\notin\pi\), then (3) prevents any split.  Indeed, within a current block \(T\), every world in \(T\cap C\) is intervened to one by (2); if this intersection is nonempty, every natural world in \(T\setminus C\) also receives one by (3), while if the intersection is empty every world is natural and receives zero.  Thus the next value is constant on \(T\).

If \(C\in\pi\), the inductive union-of-blocks property puts the whole block \(C\) inside one current block \(T_C\).  Every member of \(C\) is intervened to one, while every member of \(T_C\setminus C\) is natural and receives zero by (3).  Hence this coordinate isolates \(C\) from \(T_C\setminus C\) unless it was already isolated, and it splits no block of \(\pi\).  Other current blocks are disjoint from \(C\) and remain constant at zero.  This proves the induction invariant that the current partition is coarser than \(\pi\).

If \(\pi\) has at least two blocks, each of its blocks \(P\) is a nonempty proper subset of \([h]\), so the selector \(Z_P\) occurs.  For two distinct blocks \(P,Q\in\pi\), processing \(Z_P\) either finds them already separated or gives value one to every world in \(P\) and zero to every world in \(Q\) while they lie in a common current block.  Thus they are separated thereafter.  Consequently the final pre-\(Y\) partition is exactly \(\pi\).  If \(\pi=\{[h]\}\), every selector falls under the nonsplitting case of (3), so the same conclusion holds.  At every selector the factual predecessor tuple has its prescribed zero row, and therefore all factual pins remain satisfied.  This also proves explicitly that intervention pins at selectors never accidentally split a target block.  Completing unused rows by zero yields a legal complete-predecessor response prefix, so every one of the \(B_h\) partitions is feasible in this single binary architecture.

We now distinguish any two different reachable partitions.  Let \(\pi\neq\sigma\).  There is an ordering \((\alpha,\beta)\) of this pair and a block \(Q\in\beta\) that meets at least two blocks of \(\alpha\): otherwise each partition would refine the other and they would be equal.  Choose a block \(P\in\alpha\) such that
\[
Q\cap P\neq\varnothing,
\qquad
Q\setminus P\neq\varnothing,
\]
and define
\[
b_j=\mathbf 1\{j\in P\},
\qquad j\in[h]. \tag{4}
\]
The vector \(b\) is constant on every block of \(\alpha\) and is nonconstant on \(Q\).

Let \(q_R^{\alpha}\) denote the common complete pre-\(Y\) tuple of the worlds in an \(\alpha\)-block \(R\), for the response prefix constructed above, and define one binary response table on all predecessor tuples by
\[
 f_Y^{\star}(q)=
 \begin{cases}
 b_j, & q=q_R^{\alpha}\text{ for an }R\in\alpha\text{ and any }j\in R,\\
 0, & \text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases} \tag{5}
\]
The first case is well defined because \(b\) is constant on \(R\), and tuples belonging to different \(\alpha\)-blocks are distinct.  The factual pre-\(Y\) tuple has \(S=0\), whereas every \(q_R^{\alpha}\) has \(S=1\); hence (5) gives the factual world value zero and respects its terminal pin.  Formula (5) is therefore one legal natural-\(Y\) response-table suffix after both prefixes.

Use the terminal conjunction
\[
\gamma_b^{\circ}=\bigwedge_{j=1}^{h}\{Y_{I_j}=b_j\}. \tag{6}
\]
Every intervention pair in \(I_j\) is on a predecessor of \(Y\), \(Y\notin\operatorname{dom}(I_j)\), and there are no repeated pairs.  Thus \texttt{def:query-normalizer} only canonically orders the pairs and leaves (6) predecessor-normal.  Every \(I_j\) occurs in (6), the \(I_j\)'s are distinct, and no factual atom occurs.  Consequently normalization retains exactly
\[
\mathcal H=\{I_1,\ldots,I_h\}, \tag{7}
\]
with no augmentation by the factual context.

Appending the common table (5) to the \(\alpha\)-prefix makes every atom in (6) true, because the output on \(q_R^{\alpha}\) is the common required value on \(R\).  Appending the same table to the \(\beta\)-prefix gives one common output \(d=f_Y^{\star}(q_Q^{\beta})\) to every world in the block \(Q\).  Since (4) is nonconstant on \(Q\), some \(j\in Q\) has \(b_j\neq d\); its atom in (6) is false.  Hence the same legal suffix and the same terminal normalized conjunction accept the \(\alpha\)-prefix and reject the \(\beta\)-prefix.

Thus all \(B_h\) reachable partitions are pairwise inequivalent under \texttt{def:residual-minimality-handle}.  Every exact online continuation representation must consequently have at least \(B_h\) states on this fixed binary architecture:
\[
\rho(h)\geq B_h \qquad(h\geq2). \tag{8}
\]
For \(h=1\), there is one partition and every continuation machine has at least one state, so (8) also holds.  Combining (1) and (8) proves \(\rho(h)=B_h\).  Finally, \texttt{thm:single-conjunction-compiler} supplies the displayed \(\mathsf C_1\) running-time upper bound.  Pairwise residual inequivalence certifies the number of exact continuation states only; no step above lower-bounds transition-processing time or an unrelated decision-diagram representation.
theorem.justification: This identifies the equality partition as the coarsest worst-case exact causal continuation state, rather than merely a sufficient state.
theorem.gap: General knowledge-compilation succinctness methodology does not provide a causal Myhill--Nerode lower bound for retained intervention worlds; the binary selector construction supplies that certificate on the saturated order-only carrier.
theorem.consumer: Compiler implementations may treat the Bell-number partition count as worst-case state-optimal under the stated residual interface, while retaining the separate transition-time analysis.

prose_updates.tldr: For standard finite order-compatible recursive structural causal models with arbitrary predecessor parent subsets and shared exogenous variation, the sourced causal-order canonicalization permits sharp-bound optimization over a saturated all-predecessor response carrier. A deterministic value-preserving normalizer derives predecessor-only retained contexts from explicit unnested intervention atoms, and the equality partition of their complete prefixes is an exact continuation state. It is also worst-case residual-minimal: a self-contained binary selector construction realizes and pairwise separates all \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) partitions while keeping the factual zero cell outside the retained context set. Representative transitions yield exact conjunction and joint-score compilers whose exponential factors depend on the normalized number of worlds and score terms but not on alphabet cardinalities. Sparse traceback and one exogenous atom per positive observational cell attain the sharp cell-sum endpoints.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact order-only method proves canonical equivalence between parent-subset recursive models and complete all-predecessor response carriers, then enumerates completed response signatures before quotienting them by observational and query evaluations, leaving an alphabet-product optimization space. It does not establish either a value-preserving predecessor normal form for a prefix compiler, complete-prefix equality as an exact local continuation state, or worst-case residual minimality of that state.
project_justification.niche: Explicit unnested queries with few normalized intervention contexts but many endogenous coordinates or large alphabets admit a smaller semantic state on the equivalent canonical carrier: later unrestricted all-predecessor response rows see only which retained worlds currently share a complete input tuple. The binary selector lower bound shows that no uniformly coarser exact state exists under the declared causal residual interface.
project_justification.fill: The project keeps the standard parent-subset SCM class as its target, invokes the sourced canonical-carrier equivalence, proves deterministic normalization and equality-type continuation on that carrier, derives complete representative transitions and explicit \(h\)- and \(r\)-dependent bounds, reconstructs sparse response systems, certifies sharp endpoints for the standard class, and proves \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) by a pin-resistant binary construction. The lower bound concerns exact continuation states, not running time or all decision-diagram representations.

prose_updates.related_work: Rossetto and Antonucci, in \emph{Partial Identification under Causal Orders by Linear Programming}, establish in Theorems~1--4 and their lifted-program and constructive-sharpness results the exact order-only identified set and the equivalence that permits optimization over complete all-predecessor response signatures even when a standard recursive model has parent subsets. The present compiler takes that sourced equivalence as its interface and tightens the query-specific construction for small \(h\); it does not redefine arbitrary recursive structural causal models as saturated. Halpern supplies finite recursive causal certificates and broad satisfiability hardness, but not a world-count continuation parameter; predecessor-only retained contexts are derived by the normalization lemma rather than imposed as Halpern syntax or as a maintained assumption. Ganian, Gr\"{u}ndel, and Wietheger, in the 2025 preprint \emph{Gateways to Tractability for Satisfiability in Pearl's Causal Hierarchy}, study \(\mathrm{SAT}^{\mathrm{lin}}_{\mathrm{counterfact}}\), whose inputs are inequalities over probability terms on one common domain, and prove fixed-parameter tractability in their \(d+n\) parameter; no reduction, embedding, separation, or tightening is claimed here. Huber and coauthors, in \emph{Tractable Bounding of Counterfactual Queries by Knowledge Compilation}, compile fixed structural equations into arithmetic circuits for approximate causal-EM inner bounds; the present problem instead exactly quantifies, through the causal-order canonical carrier, over the standard parent-subset models compatible with \(p\) alone. Darwiche and Marquis supply the general distinction between succinctness and supported online operations, but no causal residual theorem; the present binary selector construction proves the Bell-state lower bound directly. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim cover arbitrary graphs and heterogeneous data through canonical polynomial programs, a broader setting excluded here. Han, Chen, and Darwiche control multi-world width when mechanisms are fully specified, whereas the current state quantifies over unknown mechanisms. Zaffalon and coauthors demonstrate the hardness of partially specified graphical models even on polytrees, explaining why prescribed sparse graphs are not absorbed into the order-only result.
prose_updates.interpretation: The equality partition forgets all numeric prefix labels and retains exactly the cross-world coincidence information that an unrestricted next response row can observe. The lower-bound family shows that every one of the \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) coincidence patterns can matter to a later causal conjunction, even with binary variables and factual zeros. This is optimality for the declared exact online residual state; it neither lower-bounds total running time nor rules out compression tailored to a fixed query or a different compilation language.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The equality partition is insufficient when a sparse parent graph is prescribed as part of the model class. In the chain \(A\to B\to Y\) without \(A\to Y\), two two-world histories can have the same partition of complete \((A,B)\) prefixes but different equality of the actual parent \(B\) supplied to \(Y\), hence different feasible future outcomes. The standard order-compatible target class allows parent subsets, but its sharp-bound optimization uses the Rossetto--Antonucci saturated canonical carrier; that equivalence does not license the same quotient after conditioning on a prescribed sparse graph. The Bell-state lower bound is correspondingly scoped to the declared saturated-carrier residual interface and does not imply an \(h\log h\) time lower bound or a lower bound for all reduced multi-valued decision diagrams. Dense input reading, explicit unnesting, and rational bit complexity are charged; prescribed sparse graphs, independence restrictions, cycles, succinct nested syntax, and experimental-table constraints are excluded.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The Rossetto--Antonucci canonical equivalence from standard order-compatible parent-subset models to the saturated all-predecessor response carrier is credited and restated only as an interface proposition. The normalization lemma, continuation theorem, representative bounds, joint truth-state compiler, sparse reconstruction, cellwise attainment, false-bit criterion, and self-contained numeric-history separation are proved within that interface. The residual result now proves the exact characterization \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) using \(h\) nonfactual retained contexts and a separate factual zero cell; it makes no \(h\log h\) time-lower-bound claim and no claim about all reduced decision diagrams. Sanity Corollary~1 records the factual reduction and credits its \(r=1\) endpoint equality to Rossetto--Antonucci without a novelty claim. The standard finite-model certificate, broad hardness, completed-response sharpness, and sample-mean inference are credited rather than claimed. Prescribed-sparse-graph, factorized-exogenous, multi-regime, and direct nested-syntax extensions remain outside scope.
